title: Grove models two-way convertibility through a centralized issuer as two independent one-way conduits with no netting
content:
A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.3.7.2.1 configures "USDG To USDC Via Paxos" on Robinhood Chain: Asset Supplied USDG, Token to Receive USDC, Token Address and Underlying Asset Address both the same USDG contract, a Paxos Deposit Address, and a single `transferAssets` RateLimitID capped at 50,000,000 USDG per day. It is the mirror image of the Ethereum "USDC To USDG Via Paxos" Instance, which has the identical shape with the assets swapped.

Grove has not modelled this as one convertibility relationship with Paxos. It has modelled two conduits, each with its own identifier, its own limit, and its own document.

The separation is correct for the risk being managed. Each direction is a distinct off-chain obligation — sending USDC and awaiting USDG is a different exposure from sending USDG and awaiting USDC, with a different asset at stake and a different settlement path. A single bidirectional limit would let capacity consumed on one leg constrain the other for no risk-related reason.

The consequence is that the limits do not net. Grove can have 50,000,000 outbound in each direction on the same day, so the daily credit extendable to Paxos across both conduits is 100,000,000 rather than 50,000,000, and no document states that combined figure.

This also completes a dependency chain worth seeing whole. Grove's Robinhood Chain Morpho position is denominated in USDG; the only documented route between USDG and the wider stablecoin world is these two Paxos conduits; and the vault Instance's own outflow RateLimitID is deferred to "a future iteration of the Grove Artifact." Exiting the Robinhood Chain position therefore runs through a centralized issuer, and the 100 million USDS total-USDG ceiling is doing more work than its placement suggests.
description: USDC To USDG on Ethereum and USDG To USDC on Robinhood Chain are separate Instances, each with its own transferAssets limit, so 50m of outbound credit in one direction never offsets the other.
